business.summary: India's largest Yum! Brands franchisee: runs KFC and Pizza Hut in its Indian territories (Sapphire Foods holds the south/west and Sri Lanka), KFC in Thailand (via a 51:49 holding company with Camas, a Temasek affiliate), KFC and Pizza Hut in Nigeria and Nepal; also Costa Coffee, New York Fries and Sanook Kitchen in India (franchisee brands), and its own brands Vaango (South Indian), Biryani By Kilo and Goila Butter Chicken (Sky Gate, bought 2025) and food courts. 2,255 stores at 30-Jun-2026 (India 1,855; Thailand 323; Nigeria 39; Nepal 38).

royaltyFY26.src: ar26 note 33 (royalty and continuing fees Rs3,634.5 mn; FY25 Rs3,349.2 mn)

segments.src: q4ppt slides 8-10; ar26 note 49 (India Rs37,521 mn, Thailand Rs16,919 mn, rest of world Rs1,675 mn). Presentation India revenue is Rs41 cr above the geographic note: removed on consolidation.

balance.src: q4ppt slide 23 (non-current lease liabilities Rs22,567 mn); Screener lease schedule (total Rs2,473 cr); ar26 KAM (intangibles)

guidance.what: Net new stores FY27: about 200-225 (standalone, all brands); KFC India 100-120; no net new Pizza Hut stores in calendar 2026
KFC SSSG of about 5-6% medium term; KFC brand contribution above 20% once ADS reaches Rs105-110k (Rs98k in Q1FY27), in about 1.5-2 years
KFC on-premise (dine-in) mix target 59-60% (57% in Q1FY27)
Biryani By Kilo to a Rs1,000 cr brand 'in the next few years' (~Rs250 cr at acquisition)

Sapphire merger completion by end-FY27; net synergies Rs210-225 cr a year at steady state (~2.5% of combined EBITDA base), ~60% in year one, 100% within two years; one-time fee to Yum! ~Rs320 cr (to be capitalised)
Tech-related changes within existing budgets; no change in capex per store from the dine-in push

history.event: Incorporated (RJ Corp group of Ravi Jaipuria; Varun Beverages is the group's PepsiCo bottler)
First Pizza Hut restaurant (Jaipur), as Yum!'s franchisee
IPO at Rs90 a share (Rs1,838 cr: fresh issue Rs440 cr; offer for sale ~Rs1,398 cr by RJ Corp and Dunearn, a Temasek subsidiary); listed at ~Rs141
Thailand: Devyani International DMCC (51% DIL, 49% Camas, a Temasek affiliate) bought Restaurants Development Co. (~280 KFC stores) for THB 4,682 mn (~Rs1,091 cr incl. shareholder loan)
Sky Gate Hospitality (Biryani By Kilo, Goila Butter Chicken) 80.72% for ~Rs420 cr, paid in 2.37 cr new shares at Rs176.78; 86.13% later; wholly owned from 7-Mar-2026

Board approves merger of Sapphire Foods into Devyani: 177 Devyani shares per 100 Sapphire shares; appointed date 1-Apr-2026; Arctic International (RJ Corp group) to buy 18.5% of Sapphire from its promoters
Manish Dawar (CFO) becomes President & Group CEO; Virag Joshi retires as CEO (stays a non-executive director); Anupam Kumar CFO; new CTO and CMO hired
NSE observation letter (no objection) on the scheme; BSE letter with no adverse observations; six months to file with the NCLT

Arctic purchase of 18.5% of Sapphire mutually terminated; Sapphire's promoter will take Devyani shares instead; CCI and NCLT approvals still pending at 30-Sep-2026; merged company would have 180.18 cr shares with the RJ Corp group at 41.99%
